Short answer: ALWAYS use an experienced model. You almost never want to use a new, fresh one. Even if you're using two brand new people. Just keep using the same model, always, for everything.

Long answer: training the model over time will expose it to more faces, more poses, more lighting, more angles, etc. Ultimately that will mean it understand the human face better, and you'll notice faster/better results over time. With my 1080 Ti and a very experienced and well-used model file, my B > A training takes very little time before it's already about as good as it's going to get, because my model knows how to mold to whatever face I throw at it without much challenge at this point. I'm at a point now where I can train for ~3 hours and have just as good of results if I trained at ~8 hours, and I owe most of that to my model file (and GPU).

I've also noticed that over time my model has been much better at recognizing blowjobs, for example. When I first started out, my BJ fakes would be super fucked up and the faces would be going nuts because my model had no idea WTF this giant dick was in front of the face all of the sudden. Months later, my model knows that's a dick, and morphs the face behind it without affecting the dick itself. My model also knows how to open mouths of lots of my B sources in BJ scenes, even if I (obviously) have no B images of the subject giving a BJ (or even eating something).
